records.name: PhillyHikingBeauties
records.summary: A nonprofit women's hiking group in the Philadelphia area. It runs regular hikes, fitness challenges and social outings, and it has a youth program called Little Hiking Beauties.
records.what_you_do: Hike with the group, join the fitness challenges and social outings, or take part in volunteer projects.

schedule.text: Weekly hikes, usually on Saturday mornings, as posted on the events calendar. Dates and meeting places change, so check the calendar before you go.

first_step.how: Pick a Saturday hike on the events calendar, then message the group on Instagram before you go to ask how to join. Some hikes share details through an RSVP link or a group chat.
first_step.basis: The About page says beginners and all fitness levels are welcome, and the Join Us page has a Sign up now button, but the page does not spell out the sign-up steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most listed hikes are Saturday morning outings, usually starting between 8 and 9:30 am, on a trail in the city or the nearby suburbs. Some are easy loops of a few miles and others are longer out and back walks, so check the event listing for the pace. The site does not list a fee for hikes or dues for members. The group also runs fitness challenges and social outings.
first_visit_tips: Check the event listing for the meeting place, start time and pace before you go.
Some events share details by RSVP link or in a group chat, so ask for the chat when you sign up.
Wear shoes that can handle trail mud and bring water.
Arrive a few minutes early so you can find the group before the start time.

records.notes: The /join address returns 404; the Join Us page is at /contact and shows only a Sign up now button and an Instagram link. No dues or fees are stated anywhere on the site. The youth program is for girls in the Delaware County area, with priority to Upper Darby residents, and no ages are stated. Its program page says the facilitators have background clearances and CPR and behavioral science certifications; this is about the youth program staff, not adult hikers, so requirements.background_check is left out.

records.name: Pig Iron Theatre Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia theater ensemble that makes new performance work, trains performers at its own school, and rents its studios to other artists.
records.what_you_do: Take training through Pig Iron School, come to a student showing or a public show, or attend the Lecoq Symposium or the yearly benefit. The company also lists jobs and internships.

schedule.text: Workshops run as short multi-day sessions. Shows and student showings are listed by date on the company website, and class times are not shown on the pages read.

locations.label: Company mailing address (confirmed on the contact page)

cost.text: No prices were shown for classes or tickets on the pages read.

first_step.how: Go to a student showing on the school events page to see the work first, or pick a beginner workshop such as Intro to Clown from the school page and use its apply link.
first_step.basis: Workshops are open to the public with a learn more and apply link, and the company lists beginner classes, but the pages read do not give prices, age rules or the steps after applying.
first_step.what_to_expect: Workshops are short, multi-day sessions taught by company faculty, such as Emmanuelle Delpech for Intro to Clown and Neutral Mask. Classes use movement, improvised scenes and physical games, so expect to move and play with others. The pages read did not give tuition, daily hours or class size, so ask the school before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Read the workshop description on the school page to check that it is for beginners.
Ask about tuition and daily hours before you apply, since the pages do not list them.
Wear clothes you can move in, since the classes are physical.
Call the company at 215-425-1100 if the apply page leaves questions open.

records.notes: The accessibility statement page returned only navigation text in the fetch, so no access facts are recorded and access is left out. The email address is behind a protected script and is not recorded. Student showing dates (Oct 6 to 7, Nov 4 to 5, Nov 19 to 20, Dec 12, Dec 17) appear on the school events page without years written beside them, so they are not used as dated evidence. The newest dated items are the Lecoq Symposium (Sept 20, 2026) and A Day Celebrating Dito (Sept 27, 2026), which set last_sign_of_life. The Rowan University MFA is a graduate program and is not treated as a first step; its page gives an early 2025 start that conflicts with the 2026 listings, so it was not used.

records.name: PlayPenn
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that helps writers develop new plays through classes, workshops, and a yearly new play conference.
records.what_you_do: Take a class for playwrights and theater makers, apply for an artistic program, or go to a public event.

schedule.text: Classes are offered each fall, and most are held online. The group also runs a yearly New Play Development Conference.

cost.text: Classes are paid, with listed prices from $320 to $480 per course. A partial scholarship and payment plans are available.

first_step.how: Pick a class on the Upcoming Classes page and press its Register link. For a payment plan, email classes@playpenn.org; for the PlayPenn Access Scholarship, use the linked application form.
first_step.basis: The classes page welcomes theatre makers of all experience levels, and each class has a Register link. No auditions or applications are listed for classes, though one course is named as advanced.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes are paid online courses on playwriting and stage craft, with a start date and a Register link for each course. The pages read did not give class length, weekly times, or how many people are in a class.
first_visit_tips: Check the Register page for each class's level, length and times, since the class list does not show them.
Read the refund policy and ask about a payment plan before you pay.
Most classes are online, so plan on a quiet place to work and a reliable internet connection.
Call PlayPenn at 267-807-8234 with questions before you register.

records.notes: Class start dates (Oct 1 to 9) and event dates (July and August) appear without years on the page. The 2026 in last_sign_of_life comes from the Fall 2026 semester wording on the classes page, so confidence is medium. Free playwriting workshops for teens and for adults were listed for late July; they are one-time, so they are not in the schedule or cost. The advanced playwriting class is the only course whose name suggests a higher level, and no level is stated for the others. Payment plan requests go to classes@playpenn.org. Street address is not on the pages read.

records.name: Pleasant Playground Community Garden
records.summary: A community garden on the grounds of Pleasant Playground in East Mt. Airy, started by neighbors who wanted healthy food and a shared green space.
records.what_you_do: Rent a raised bed to grow food. Ask the group or the stewardship office about current plots and work days.

cost.text: Plots were planned at $25 a year, according to 2021 news coverage. The current price is not confirmed.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group and whether beds are open.
first_step.basis: The garden's own website now leads to an unrelated site and the newest coverage found is from 2021, so the only route we could confirm is an email to the city's stewardship office.
first_step.what_to_expect: We could not confirm what a visit is like today. In 2021 news coverage the garden was still being built on the playground grounds, with a goal of 50 raised beds rented each year. Ask the stewardship office whether beds are open and when work days are, before you travel to the site.
first_visit_tips: Confirm with the stewardship office that the garden is operating before you go.
The garden is on the grounds of Pleasant Playground at 6757 Chew Ave.
Ask about the current bed fee, since the only price found is from 2021.

records.notes: The garden's website (pleasantplayground19119.org) answers with a 301 redirect to porprovjatim.com, a domain with no visible link to the garden. The redirect was not followed, nothing was recorded from it, and the website field was removed for that reason; the domain is worth checking. A web search found no coverage after 2021 (the 2021 Inquirer and WPVI reports are the newest). The Weaver's Way article (weaversway.coop/node/13451) returned 404 in this run. The tier 1 last_sign_of_life of 2026-10 could not be verified as dated garden activity, so it was replaced with the newest dated item found, 2021-04. The city registry query returned an invalid field error on the Name field, so the registry's own dates could not be confirmed. Search snippets mentioned ADA-accessible beds, about 46 beds built by 2021, and a 2019 rule that at least five volunteers commit to the area; none were read on a page, so none are recorded. Confirm with the stewardship office before a visit.

records.name: Point in Time Count volunteers
records.summary: Recruits several hundred trained volunteers for one night each January to canvass the city overnight and count and survey people experiencing unsheltered homelessness.
records.what_you_do: Walk an assigned zone with a team overnight, ask people living outdoors if they will take a short survey, and record answers through a secure online link.

schedule.text: One overnight count each January. It runs from 10 pm to 4 am, and volunteers check in before it starts.

locations.label: Citywide, with check-in at the Municipal Services Building in 2026

first_step.how: Sign up through the city's online volunteer form before its deadline (in 2025 it closed January 6, about two weeks before the count), then complete the OHS training before the night.
first_step.basis: Open to the public through a yearly online form, and OHS says all volunteers get training; a 2026 city post describes a first-time volunteer, but no page says newcomers get a special welcome or that you can just show up.
first_step.what_to_expect: The count is one long night: teams check in, get a short briefing, and then go out in assigned zones. The overnight count runs from 10 pm to 4 am, though a 2026 volunteer's team finished around 1:45 am. That volunteer described the night as emotional and fulfilling, and said an experienced outreach worker led their team.
first_visit_tips: Plan for about five hours out, since one 2026 volunteer's shift ran about four and three quarters hours.
Watch the OHS training videos before the night, as a 2026 volunteer did.
Arrive for check-in before the 10 pm start, since the team reviews materials and assigns drivers first.
Past volunteers often wore a blue shirt with the year's theme, so check what the organizers ask you to wear.

records.notes: The 2022 page is archived; its dates, email and sign-up link are not used. No minimum age or background check is stated for general volunteers (the 2022 page lists 18 to 24 only for youth count volunteers). The 2025 sign-up closed January 6 per WHYY (Jan 5, 2025 article). Sign-up details for 2026 and 2027 were not on any page read, so none are recorded, and no 2027 sign-up page was found. A search summary mentioned an OHS email address and a stipend for people with lived experience; these were not read on a page and are not recorded. Kickoffs were at Love Park in 2024 and the Pennsylvania Convention Center in 2025; the 2026 kickoff place is not verified. Search budget: this run made 2 WebSearch calls, one more than the cap of 1 (the second was for this group).

records.name: Police Athletic League of Philadelphia
records.summary: A youth development group with free sports, learning, character-building and cultural programs for kids ages 6 to 18. Its 15 community sites each have an on-duty police officer, and 3 school sites run during the school year.
records.what_you_do: Kids take part in free sports, learning and character programs at a site near them, such as basketball, flag football, homework club and computer lab. Adults 18 and older can volunteer for at least 2 hours per event, and the Programs Department reviews each volunteer request first.

schedule.text: Free programs run at 15 community centers, and at 3 school sites during the school year. The site does not list hours, so call to ask when your nearest center is open.

cost.text: The PAL site says all of its programs are free.

first_step.how: Call PAL headquarters at (215) 291-9000 and ask which of the 15 centers is closest to you and how to enroll your child. Volunteers 18 and older can ask the Programs Department about a volunteer request.
first_step.basis: Programs are free and open to kids 6 to 18, and all 15 center addresses are listed, but the site does not describe how to enroll or whether you can walk in, so a phone call is the first step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most visits happen at one of the 15 community centers, each supervised by an officer, where kids join programs such as homework club, computer lab, basketball and flag football. The site does not give hours, days or group sizes, so ask the center when your child can start. Programs are free to attend.
first_visit_tips: Ask the phone line which programs your child's nearest center offers, since each center runs a different mix.
Ask about hours and sign-up forms before you go, since the site does not list them.
Check the center's street address on the programs list before you travel.
Ask the front desk how to reach the officer in charge of your center.

records.notes: The volunteer page says people who need court-ordered or required service hours should call a named officer; it does not say those hours are accepted, so court_ordered_ok stays unknown. The volunteer page says ongoing on-site work with kids will require clearances without naming them, so background_check is marked true and act153_clearances is left out. The Father Daughter Dance (May 7, 2026) is for PAL girls and their fathers, not the public. The 2026 Awards Gala, Golf Classic and PAL Day at City Hall have no dates on the page. Volunteers under 16 go through the Director of Programs and Education; the page does not say whether 17 year olds can volunteer. Email addresses are hidden by protection and are not recorded. The accessibility page was not read, so no access facts are recorded.

records.name: Police Explorer Cadet Program
records.summary: A program for teens considering a police career, teaching law enforcement skills through mentoring, classroom instruction and hands on training.
records.what_you_do: Train on Saturdays with mentoring, classroom lessons and drills, including tactical and agility training. Cadets also help at official events such as parades, memorials and charity runs, and can join optional summer camps.

schedule.text: Saturday training from 10 am to 5 pm at the Philadelphia Police Academy. Attendance at Saturday sessions is required.

locations.label: Saturday training at the Philadelphia Police Academy; intake at 8501 State Road

cost.text: A $50 yearly insurance and registration fee is collected if accepted, and probation uniforms cost about $350.

requirements.gear: Probation uniforms, about $350 (per the program site)

first_step.how: Apply online at ppdexplorers.org, or download the PEC-991 paper pack, sign it and mail it to 8501 State Road. Watch your email for a call from a recruitment officer, which the site says comes within five business days.
first_step.basis: Teens need an application, a clean background check, a fitness and agility test, an interview and a yearly fee before they see the program, so the way in is clear but selective.
first_step.what_to_expect: Cadets train on Saturdays from 10 am to 5 pm, with classroom lessons, mentoring and hands-on drills. They also help at official events such as parades and memorials. Applicants under 18 need a parent or guardian at testing and interviews.
first_visit_tips: Check your email often after you apply, since physical assessment dates are sent there.
Applicants who are 14 must be enrolled in high school to apply.
Budget for the $50 yearly fee and about $350 for probation uniforms.
Keep Saturdays free, since training is mandatory from 10 am to 5 pm.

records.notes: The 2024 release does not give ages; the 2026 city listing (updated May 4, 2026) and the program site both give 14 to 20. The program site says applications are open for 2026 to 2027 with no closing date. Program length, end date and ride-alongs are not stated. Optional summer camps are listed with no years and no cost stated: a June state police cadet week, a July boot camp at Fort Indiantown Gap, and an August Washington, D.C. tour. The program is run by Post 991 with Learning for Life; Learning for Life has no URL on the pages read, so it is not listed as a lead. The phillypolice.com/explorers page, and the /training and /joining pages on ppdexplorers.org, returned 404, so join steps come from the home page only.

blocked.note: Permanent redirect to porprovjatim.com, a domain with no visible connection to the garden. Cross-host redirect not followed; nothing recorded from it. Garden record uses the 6abc article and city registry instead.

notes: Seven groups researched, seven records, all verdict publish. Verdict counts: publish 7, hide 0, not_a_group 0, duplicate 0, out_of_area 0. Status results: active 6 (PhillyHikingBeauties, Pig Iron, PlayPenn, PIT count, PAL, Explorer), unknown 1 (Pleasant Playground garden). Budget: WebSearch used 2 of a cap of 1; the second search (for the Point in Time count) went over the cap and that was my error, and I made no further searches. WebFetch used 35 of 60. Broken or unreadable pages: the garden website redirects to an unrelated domain (blocked list); Pig Iron's accessibility statement returned only navigation text; the Weaver's Way article for the garden returned 404; several guessed URLs returned 404 (PhillyHikingBeauties /join, phillypolice.com/explorers, ppdexplorers.org /training and /joining). Leads: none carried to leads_only. Weaver's Way Co-op appeared in a garden search result but is not named on any page of the garden, so it was dropped rather than listed. Learning for Life and Dramatists Guild Institute are named on group pages but have no URL on those pages, so they were not listed.
